#1704. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Also, it was Pulisics’ pass to Moreira that set-up Cisse’s goal. If were recognizing “hockey assists” then Pulisic’s pass to Moreira was also world-class. Not to be a wet-blanket, but Moreira and Cisse need to develop composure on the ball. Too often Moreira would negate his speed on the ball by dribbling into multiple defenders without looking to pass to an open teammate. Against the top teams Milan will not have as many goal scoring opportunities as they did on Sunday so now is the time to work on finding the open man in the final third.

So young players with potential, need to learn to be better and realise thier potential.

It was a pass in a 3v3 counter-attack situation. Great pass but Modric took out 5 defenders with 1 move. That is why it is world class and Pulisic pass is not mentioned as much.

Did anyone notice how Pulisic slowed down his run, thus letting Ramos reach the penalty box earlier and score his long awaited goal? Such a team player..

He’s always been that guy. Sometimes I wish he can be more ‘selfish’. Another example is the penalty fiasco with Tammy back then.

Yet some people here have called him selfish many times – especially last season when he wasn’t scoring. But then again, those same people praised Leao and probably thought he was Ballon d’Or material. LOL. 🤦‍♂️😂😂😂

Yes. I’d say it was as much about letting Ramos score as it was about “arriving” in the box late, setting up a cut back score, which he learned from Frank Lampard. Both are good things.

#1703. ‘One of the best’: Sandro Tonali issues verdict on Tottenham star after superb Ipswich showing

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali has hailed Tottenham team-mate Destiny Udogie as “one of the best” left-backs.

The Italian pair were already familiar with one another before Tonali’s big-money move to north London from Newcastle United in the summer for a fee worth £100million.

They had first played together in at Under-21 level on the international stage, before reuniting for the senior Azzurri side and at club level.

Udogie, who was told by manager Roberto De Zerbi what he must do to start more games, was given the nod from the off against Ipswich Town last time out, as Spurs won 2-0 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The left-back impressed behind Luca Williams-Barnett, with the young star netting his first goal for the club on his first senior start.

Udogie, meanwhile, was making just his fifth start of the campaign amid injury problems.

He has also had to contend with former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson arriving to add competition in his position after Djed Spence’s departure for Inter Milan.

On Udogie, Tonali told Stadium Astro: "He's a lovely guy. He's I think he's one of the best left wing[-backs]. He has to work every day now. He has a little bit of a problem with injuries, but I think he's a good guy for us.

"I think he played one of the best games against Manchester [United], and he pushes up like a high winger, and I love him because he's always happy.

"If you win, he's happy; if you lose, he's happy. If you have a bad day, he's happy, and I think when I look at him, I'm happy."

#1702. Arsenal injury, suspension list and return dates vs. Man City: David Raya, Bukayo Saka, Martin Zubimendi latest

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 08:36

Seeking to surge nine points clear of Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table, Arsenal welcome Enzo Maresca's men to the Emirates Stadium for Sunday's main event.

The Gunners were not punished for dropping points in their 2-2 draw with Newcastle United last weekend, thanks to the Sky Blues' own slip-up against Fulham and Brighton & Hove Albion's shock loss at Hull City.

The champions therefore sit six points clear of both blue-clad rivals after 11 matches, but the Emirates faithful experienced draw deja vu in Tuesday's 1-1 stalemate with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Arsenal's latest injury and suspension news for their clash with Man City, who also had to settle for a point in Europe last time out, being held to a 2-2 draw at home to Napoli.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Manchester City)

David Raya appeared to have done serious damage to his shoulder when he was taken off against Newcastle, but Arsenal's number one has avoided a major injury and will not require surgery.

Arteta has not ruled him out of Sunday's game just yet, but he is facing a race against time to prove his fitness.

Possible return date: December 20 (vs. Manchester United)

Bukayo Saka suffered a severe quadriceps injury in October's 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich, and the England international will not return to action until just before Christmas in the best-case scenario.

Possible return date: December 20 (vs. Manchester United)

Martin Zubimendi pulled his hamstring during Spain's Nations League defeat to England earlier this month, and like Saka, the midfielder faces another few weeks in the medical bay.

Arsenal have no players suspended for this game, as Max Dowman has now completed a three-match ban following his red card against Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup.

#1701. Manchester United dealt transfer blow as ‘January target’ signs new contract

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has shut down all rumours of a Leeds United exit by signing a new contract at Elland Road.

The striker had been linked with a move away from the Yorkshire club - with several outlets identifying him as a potential target for Manchester United - but he will remain a White after penning a new two-and-a-half-year deal.

The No9 has spent the past two seasons at Leeds, joining Daniel Farke’s side upon their return to the Premier League last term.

He has established himself as the club’s first-choice striker since his free transfer move after his contract at Everton expired at the end of the 2024-25 campaign.

The England international has forced his way into Thomas Tuchel’s plans for the most recent Nations League games, and he could well have a chance to impress up top with Harry Kane sidelined after tearing his ankle ligaments.

Calvert-Lewin netted 15 goals in his first season in a Leeds shirt, and he has six strikes in 13 matches so far this term.

His hot run of goalscoring form has seen him linked with a move to Old Trafford, where new manager Mauricio Pochettino is thought to be keen on reinforcing his attack after injuries to Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford.

Calvert-Lewin was one of the names that was reportedly on the Red Devils’ shortlist ahead of the January transfer window, but his decision to sign a new contract at Elland Road will come as a major blow to Pochettino as he looks to shape United’s squad in his image.

#1700. Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal; Man Utd twist; Chelsea latest

The January transfer window is approaching fast, with Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham all striving to get some early signings over the line. Arsenal have been told Bournemouth’s decision over selling top target Eli Junior Kroupi, while they continue to scout Antonio Nusa amid new links to the likes of Carlos Forbs and Tornike Kvaratskhelia.

Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, while they are also said to be contemplating a surprise return to Anfield for Jarell Quansah. Manchester United are looking at both Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins as they try to strengthen their dreadful defence, with a new striker also high on Mauricio Pochettino’s shortlist with a rumoured £50million budget - including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has agreed a new contract with Leeds.

Chelsea are renewing their push to win the fierce battle for Alex Scott as Paris Saint-Germain pursue Estevao, while Tottenham have signed former West Ham youngster Isaac Allen ahead of Arsenal as they also scout Vangelis Pavlidis and Hakan Calhanoglu. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Richarlison is open to moving to Saudi Arabia to end his Tottenham exile.

The striker has been frozen out at Spurs by manager Roberto De Zerbi after failing to agree a summer exit.

Everton, Vasco da Gama and Trabzonspor were all said to have explored deals for Richarlison, who ended up staying put at Spurs despite being left out of De Zerbi's Premier League squad.

Manchester United fans will be dismayed by reports that Mauricio Pochettino will have just £50million to improve his squad during the January transfer window.

A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

The second window of the season often leads to inflated prices, with clubs capitalising upon other teams’ struggles and desperate need for new players.

Omar Marmoush has hailed Luca Williams-Barnett as “unbelievable” and believes the teen sensation has a “very promising future ahead of him”.

The 18-year-old scored one, and set up another, on his full debut for Tottenham in their 2-0 home win against Ipswich last weekend.

Williams-Barnett has since signed a new deal to commit his future to Spurs until 2031.

Tosin Adarabioyo has said that “no-one can chat s***” about his former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer despite the England international’s struggles this season.

Palmer has scored five times in his 13 appearances across the Premier League and Carabao Cup this term, adding three assists in the top flight.

Sandro Tonali has hailed Tottenham team-mate Destiny Udogie as “one of the best” left-backs.

The Italian pair were already familiar with one another before Tonali’s big-money move to north London from Newcastle United in the summer for a fee worth £100million.

They had first played together in at Under-21 level on the international stage, before reuniting for the senior Azzurri side and at club level.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has shut down all rumours of a Leeds United exit by signing a new contract at Elland Road.

The striker had been linked with a move away from the Yorkshire club - with several outlets identifying him as a potential target for Manchester United - but he will remain a White after penning a new two-and-a-half-year deal.

Paris Saint-Germain could push to sign Chelsea star Estevao or rival Arsenal for Antonio Nusa, reports claim.

Reigning back-to-back European champions PSG are on the lookout for further attacking reinforcements in the January transfer window as they seek to ensure another trophy-laden campaign under Luis Enrique.

According to Diario AS in Spain, the French giants are interested in offering the little-used Estevao an escape route from Stamford Bridge.

The Brazilian is said to feature on a shortlist along with Arsenal target Nusa - of RB Leipzig - and Bayern Munich’s Luis Diaz.

Jarell Quansah could make a surprise return to Liverpool.

The versatile defender has continued to flourish since leaving Anfield for Bayer Leverkusen in a £35m deal in the summer of 2025, impressing in the Bundesliga and becoming a favoured option of England boss Thomas Tuchel.

That has led to reported interest in a swift Premier League comeback from the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea.

According to TEAMtalk, Liverpool are keeping a close eye on Quansah’s progress in Germany and haven’t ruled out activating a buy-back clause that is valid until next summer and believed to be valued at just over £50m.

Teenage defender Isaac Allen has confirmed that he has joined Tottenham after leaving rivals West Ham in the summer, writes Sam Tabuteau.

In August, reports claimed that Spurs had beaten Arsenal to Allen’s signature, and the 15-year-old has now announced the move on social media.

The England U15s captain wrote in a post on Instagram: “Happy to be signed with Tottenham.”

Allen, who can operate either at centre-back or in defensive midfield, is regarded as one of the most promising young talents in England and his arrival continues Spurs’ busy youth recruitment strategy.

Tottenham look to be keeping a close eye on Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis.

Spurs are known to be on the lookout for a new forward ahead of the January transfer window to help boost Roberto De Zerbi’s inconsistent attack.

They have been linked with a swoop for Pavlidis for some time now, with Portuguese outlet Record reporting that they dispatched scouts to watch the Greek international in action again this week.

#1698. Manchester United handed huge transfer boost as left-back ‘wants £50m move’

Manchester United have been handed a boost in their transfer pursuit of Maxi Araujo.

That is according to Sport Witness, who claim that the Red Devils could seal a deal worth between €50million and €60m for the left-back.

The left-sided full-back position has been a source of real problems for United, and particularly for new manager Mauricio Pochettino, who is still awaiting his first win in charge since his arrival last week.

The Argentine took the reins at Old Trafford last Wednesday, leading his side to Anfield for a 4-0 debut demolition before a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In that Sporting side was Araujo, 26, who is believed to be open to a move to the Premier League.

The Uruguay international has previously been linked with a switch to the north west amid the pending expiry of Luke Shaw’s contract and Harry Amass’ uncertain future at Old Trafford.

Now, Sport Witness claim that United’s scouts took advantage of their fixture in the Portuguese capital to make a proper assessment of Araujo, with there thought to be appreciation of the player.

The Uruguayan is understood to have a €80m release clause in his contract at the Primeira Liga outfit, but it is believed that United would be able to negotiate the asking price down.

In Shaw’s injury-hit absence this term, Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick was forced to field natural right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui on the left side of defence, while Pochettino has favoured centre-half Lisandro Martinez in that position since he came in.

#1696. Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad: Thomas Frank claims first win as Eagles complete Europa League comeback

Crystal Palace delivered Thomas Frank a first victory after they came back to beat 10-man Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.

Dean Henderson was kept busy in the first half, making several stops to ensure it was all to play for after the break in south London, where Frank took charge of a home game for the first time.

Mamadou Sarr broke the deadlock in the 66th minute, but the contest turned on its head when Jon Martin was sent off with a second yellow card six minutes later.

Jean-Philippe Mateta fired in the penalty before second-half substitute Dwight McNeil tapped home from Jorgen Strand Larsen’s overhead kick.

Yeremy Pino had a chance to put the game away with a stoppage-time penalty but he was denied by Unai Marrero, and the hosts had to grind out a nervy finish.

The result moves the Eagles into a play-off position, after starting the evening just outside of it, in 25th.

Frank once again elected to employ a back four, as he did in his first game in charge, their 3-2 Premier League loss at Coventry.

The first chance came after a cagey first 10 minutes when the hosts gave the ball away and it fell to Benat Turrientes, who drew Henderson into a save from distance.

Henderson was then called back into action, twice denying the ever-threatening Goncalo Guedes, who was teed up by Mikel Oyarzabal’s through ball.

Palace’s best opportunity came on the stroke of half-time via a Richards throw-in, glanced on by Axel Disasi and nodded over by Mateta.

The hosts were lucky not to concede five minutes after the restart, Guedes once again at the heart of it when he laid the ball on a plate for Oyarzabal, who was one-on-one with Henderson about eight yards out but fired straight at the Eagles keeper.

Henderson made his fifth save of the night, reacting quickly to deny Jon Gorrotxategi, and the visitors remained in the driver’s seat as the hour approached and Frank made his first substitution, replacing Eddie Nketiah with McNeil.

The breakthrough for Sociedad was the product of a patient build-up ending in Job Ochieng’s low pass for Sarr, who tapped it home.

The sides were level six minutes later. Palace were awarded a penalty after Martin – who was shown a second yellow card – tugged down Mateta, and the France striker made no mistake, burying the ball past Unai Marrero.

McNeil’s winner was the product of another acrobatic assist from fellow substitute Strand Larsen, whose scorpion kick teed up Pino at Coventry.

This time it was an overhead kick, which was heading wide of the goal but McNeil pounced at the post to poke it home.

Palace were awarded a second penalty when Soler was charged with a handball, but Marrero was equal to it, giving the visitors a fighting chance at a last-gasp leveller.

But Henderson produced his biggest save of the night, denying Orri Oskarsson at the death to preserve a much-needed Palace win.

#1695. Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

The joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

She’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

It has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

Scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

Only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year plan, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

They want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

Having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.

#1693. GdS: ‘Numbers like Kaka’ – why Rabiot is so important to Milan with renewal imminent

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot said after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this new era.

The former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

With five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn

He is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Amorim said after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”

Speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

“At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s important for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

“I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”

The renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the new year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

Now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

#1692. Why are Premier League games kicking off at 2.05pm on Sunday? Liverpool and Tottenham kick-off times explained

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sunday’s Premier League games will be kicking off at slightly weird times this weekend.

Tottenham and Liverpool will be affected, while Arsenal take on Manchester City in the normal 4.30pm GMT tea-time kick-off later in the afternoon.

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, fresh off their 4-0 win over fierce rivals Manchester United, are in Merseyside derby action against Everton.

Spurs take on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light, while Crystal Palace and Fulham are both at home, with Hull City and Bournemouth travelling to the capital.

Brighton and Hove Albion also take on Newcastle United at the Amex Stadium.

The two sides that have not had their kick-off time changed are Arsenal and City, who collide in a heavyweight clash at the Emirates Stadium, with neither side coming into it off the back of a victory.

The Gunners were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund in midweek, following on from their late 2-2 stalemate at Newcastle last weekend.

City, meanwhile, were also frustrated by Fulham at home and then drew 2-2 with Napoli in midweek.

The reason for the weird kick-off times this weekend is because there is no game on Saturday lunchtime.

That slot was supposed to be for Everton hosting Liverpool, but that game has been moved to Sunday, where the game will kick-off at 12pm GMT at the Hill Dickenson Stadium.

Because that match is kicking off at 12 noon, the 2pm kick-offs have been pushed back by five minutes to try and ensure that there is no overlap between the earlier fixture and the four afternoon games.

It also means that the 2.05pm matches are unlikely to clash with the 4.30pm game.

The Europa League and Conference League have also been a factor, with the English top flight stopping clubs from playing twice within 60 hours of each match.

As a result, Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton - all in action on the continent on Thursday - are obligated to play their next matches on Sunday.

#1690. Thomas Frank identifies Crystal Palace ‘turning point’ as former Tottenham boss claims first win

Thomas Frank believes his first win as Crystal Palace manager can be a “turning point” in the club’s season.

Palace sit bottom of the Premier League table but tasted victory for the first time in Frank’s tenure with a 2-1 win over 10-man Real Sociedad in his second game in charge.

The Eagles came from behind after trailing to a second-half goal by Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr.

But Jean-Philippe Mateta levelled from the penalty spot after Jon Martin was shown a second yellow card and sent off for the side sat fifth in La Liga.

Palace then scored their eventual winner through substitute Dwight McNeil but almost threw it away when Dean Henderson was required to make a last-gasp save after Yeremy Pino had seen the Eagles’ second spot-kick of the night saved.

Palace’s victory came five days after their 3-2 defeat at Coventry in Frank’s first match in charge.

“In the second half I felt we kept the ball much better,” Frank said after his side’s victory on Thursday.

“What I really liked was the belief from the players. It is so important to keep doing the right things and keep believing.”

Palace were guilty of giving the ball away in poor errors and handing Sociedad some cheap chances despite eventually closing out a victory.

Frank said: “We should just control that game. But we probably don’t have the confidence right now.

Asked whether the win against Sociedad can be a turning point in a so-far difficult season for the south Londoners, Frank replied: “I think it could be. But we need to follow it up, of course, with a good performance against Hull on Sunday. But there were a lot of positives from this game.”

#1688. Xabi Alonso hits back at Jamie Carragher criticism as ‘responsibility’ claimed for Chelsea defending

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso says he takes the “whole responsibility” for Chelsea’s dismal defending but disagrees with his friend Jamie Carragher that Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill will never be a good enough centre-back pairing for the Blues.

The defeat exposed further weaknesses in Alonso’s defence and proved the worst possible response to their disappointing previous outing, the 1-0 defeat to Sunderland before the international break.

Chelsea head to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest on Friday night eager to get back to winning ways.

Analysing the Leeds loss, Carragher said on Sky Sports: “Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League.”

Speaking about Fofana and Colwill, he added: “As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.”

Asked whether he had seen these comments from his former Liverpool team-mate, Alonso said he had not, before adding: “I must disagree. I disagree with Carra. For sure, you can have bad games. We were not good [against Leeds]. But I think I’ve seen them [Colwill and Fofana] play well, and I’ve seen them show good levels.

“This is the goal and the challenge – to be consistent in the performance and to be consistent in the basics and not to drop in certain games when we are facing a tough opponent.”

Alonso, speaking more broadly about Chelsea’s poor defending, added: “There are no excuses not to do better. We are in the process. Taking steps, taking a step forward but until it is totally in the DNA of the team it takes time.

“I take the whole responsibility of the team and how they perform. We need to show [improvement against Forest], not just talk. Talk is cheap. It’s about performing on the pitch.

“We want to be back on that more solid feeling that we had. This was hopefully one-[off], and we don’t want to repeat it.”

#1687. Kevin De Bruyne insists potential punishment over Man City's guilty verdict will not tarnish his old club's achievements under Pep Guardiola - or diminish his 'love' for the owners

Published: 16:01 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:04 EST, 23 November 2026

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne said. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal

‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most important thing.’

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a new contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

All eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

Maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca said.

‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’

#1683. Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y

"That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young said on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

4 - Brian Brobbey is the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler v Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt v Man Utd in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku v Man Utd in May 2013.Unstoppable. pic.twitter.com/vygVYazIQD

Maresca’s side maintain their immaculate record, but boy were they made to work for it this afternoon.

Sunderland are still 5-3 down but have not given up the ghost. Surely the best match of the season so far?

It ends goalless at Elland Road after Mitchell’s goal was disallowed for offside. Kamada went close to breaking the deadlock in the final stages...

Daichi Kamada can't guide his header on target! ❌ pic.twitter.com/AgKM6Q9apq

Bournemouth lose at the Vitality for the first time in 13 matches as Iraola makes a winning return to the South Coast. Liverpool were hardly impressive, but to their credit they managed the final stages of this match with a minimum of fuss.

Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium with a win! ✅ pic.twitter.com/FSgvE6EGFB

Bournemouth are awarded a corner but Brooks’ delivery goes straight into the inviting gloves of Alisson.

Koumas pressures Petrovic, but the goalkeeper shows off some tidy footwork to escape the danger.

Bournemouth cannot get out though, and Petrovic is forced into a routine save off Koumas moments later.

Bournemouth win a free-kick in a dangerous position after a handball, but Scott cannot get his strike up and down fast enough and it sails over.

Haaland gets in on the act, but only after a VAR check. That should be that...

Erling Haaland has now scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the Premier League ✅⚽ pic.twitter.com/X9uqcrgbwk

Araujo gets his pocket picked in the corner but Jebbison cannot compose himself and blasts his cross off the other side of the pitch.

Liverpool go the other way and win a corner, but Mac Allister puts too much air on his delivery and it is easily dealt with.

Rayan wins a free-kick as he holds off Kerkez on the halfway line. Bournemouth then switch play to the far side but Truffert’s speculative effort flies well over the bar.

Nyoni shows off his composure on the ball, playing simple passes on the half-turn to keep play flowing. The midfield area is quite congested, which suits Liverpool at this point in the game.

Liverpool are baiting Bournemouth’s press in an attempt to play around their front line. They are doing a good job at holding on to the ball and frustrating their opponents, for now.

Gravenberch and Koumas are on for Gakpo and Isak.

Brooks has brought some energy to Bournemouth’s forays down the left. He attempts to slip a ball into the left channel but Nyoni is wise to it and positions himself perfectly to cut it out.

Liverpool have dropped deep and Bournemouth wait patiently for an opening. They eventually find Tavernier in the left half-space but his cross flies over everyone.

That is his last contribution to the match as Rose rings the changes: Tavernier, Smith and Christie make way for Brooks, Jebbison and Cook.

Truffert spins in a teasing ball from the left but Jacquet does well to flick the ball away from the danger zone.

Wirtz and Barcola make way for Nyoni and Munoz. Quiet afternoon from both of the outgoing players.

A stunning block from Hill prevents Isak pulling trigger as he looked to have the goal in his sights.

Truffert clears the resulting corner to safety.

Isak is concentrating his efforts in more central areas and here he almost gets played in behind but the ball just runs away from him. Better.

Worth mentioning that Jacquet has been fantastic in all phases of the game. Plenty of advanced regains and tidy passes forward.

It’s raining goals in Manchester and no prizes for guessing who has scored for Sunderland. Brobbey has his hat-trick.

Brobbey has his hat-trick and the look on Enzo Maresca’s face as he assesses the defending from his team. They’ve been great pouring forward, less so trying to stymie Sunderand’s attack. But this is one of those games where you just sit back and enjoy the unfolding drama. It’s been so good from both teams.

Semenyo gets his second goal of the afternoon to extend the league leaders’ advantage.

Chance! Jacquet jumps and wins the ball well inside Bournemouth’s half and his intervention sends the ball into Isak’s path. The forward just drags his effort wide and turns out he was in an offside postion anyhow.

What an afternoon this is turning out to be. There have been more slices than on an erratic day on the local municipal golf course and Ronald Araujo is the latest to be afflicted by the condition. None of that will matter to Andoni Iraola, though, as Alexander Isak’s fourth goal in four Premier League games has given Liverpool a huge advantage. They haven’t played with fluency but the breakthrough was significant.

Isak opens the scoring at the Vitality, finally getting into the box and sweeping in from close range. So much credit has to go to Gakpo who tiptoes past two Bournemouth defenders by the touchline before spearing a cross infield, and while he may not be attributed with the assist owing to a touch off Wirtz, his delivery makes it all the way through to Isak who taps in.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4

Adams has been superb as one of Bournemouth’s two midfield sentries. Kerkez looks to have been played into the left channel but the American swoops in and shields the ball out of play before staring down his Hungarian opponent.

Mitchell thinks he’s given the visitors the lead but his goal is ruled out for offside.

Tyrick Mitchell's opener is disallowed for an offside in the build up! ❌ pic.twitter.com/7y975TxaUj

Liverpool give up possession in Bournemouth’s half and Christie strides forward releasing Rayan before continuing his run to the near post. The Brazilian picks out his team-mate but Christie gets too strong a contact on the ball and the ball sails wide.

Truffert passes the ball straight to Gakpo inside his own box but Adams is on the scene in a flash and snaps into a tackle and takes the ball away from the Liverpool forward.

The second has already settled into a holding pattern, with neither side creating much. Isak makes a run down the right hand side and, with players loaded in the box, he blasts the ball high into the sky and beyond his team-mates. That pretty much sums things up.

Wirtz has given the ball away twice in the first minute of the second half. Carragher is on Sky Sports commentary duties and he says he’s surprised to see him back out on the pitch.

Szoboszlai concedes a foul on the far side but the subsequent delivery is too heavy and sails over everyone.

No half-time changes from either manager.

3 - This is the first time that @ManCity have taken the lead three times in the first half of a Premier League match.Overall, it's just the seventh time in competition history that a side has gone ahead on three separate occasions in a first half.Canvas. pic.twitter.com/JaQ4qDarls

Isak’s first-half heatmap makes for interesting reading. The good news, for Liverpool fans, is that he’s stationed himself predominantly in the final third. The bad news... those positions have been everywhere but the box.

There must be significant temptation to drift out to the wide areas and drop deep when the ball is not coming to you, but surely Liverpool need their No 9 closer to Bournemouth’s goal?

Bournemouth 0 Liverpool 0Leeds United 0 Crystal Palace 0 Manchester City 3 Sunderland 2

Big chance missed from Haaland of all people to make it 4-2 to City in what has been a pulsating, spell-binding first 45 minutes. It’s fast, furious and a helluva lot of fun to watch. Brilliant from Ndiaye to tee up Haaland who shoots wide of a post. A game for attackers shall we say ...

There are significant advantages to having a goalkeeper who is 6ft 5in with long arms and massive hands. Brobbey’s shot cannons off Guehi and would have looped over a number of goalkeeper but Donnarumma sticks out a giant arm to help nudge the ball over the bar and keep City 3-2 in front in the fifth minute of first half stoppages

Not a pretty half from the returning Iraola’s side, who will need to be much better in the second period to challenge for the three points.

Bournemouth have dropped points late on in a number of matches this season and will perhaps rue not being able to capitalise on their early advantage.

City are in front. Again. Semenyo this time, he fires the ball beyond Roefs having collected a loose ball int he box.

Antoine Semenyo gets his first goal of the season! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/1n2W5Cyxz0

A relatively slick Liverpool move sees the ball worked out to Araujo on the right who has minded to bomb on with increasing frequency, and while he’s able to win a corner, Szoboszlai’s delivery is cleared with a minimum of fuss.

Iraola came into this game saying that his side held an advantage having played two days earlier than Bournemouth in midweek. You would never have guessed it from what we have witnessed here today.

And right on cue, a frustrated Isak attempts a specultative effort from range which sails high and wide.

Sunderland are level again as Brobbey scores after lengthy VAR check for offside.

Sunderland fans sing “F--- VAR” and City fans boo the delay while they both awaited the verdict, which has now gone Sunderland’s way

Brian Brobbey levels it AGAIN! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/YvelzwnmY8

Can’t hold a lead today City. Wow, Sunderland are level again in an instant and it’s that man Brobbey again. There’s a VAR check going on to check for offside

So, this is not a rush to make a sweeping criticism, it’s simply an observation. But Liverpool fans will be looking at Bradley Barcola and  waiting to see that first burst, that moment of electricity, that has showed why they bought him. It’s like you look for a touch, a pass, a moment of skill. He’s just had a shot saved but it all seems very tentative for him at the moment. And that is what he needs - a moment.

Jacquet does brilliantly to close down Christie as the Scot was stealing into the box and looking to pull the trigger.

Chances! Barcola forces Petrovic into an awkward-looking save, before follow-up efforts from Wirtz and Gakpo are charged down.

Mac Allister is fouled 25 yards out moments later and Szoboszlai gets another go. Here, he drags his effort just wide.

It’s all happening at the Etihad. Cherki restores City’s lead with his third Premier League goal of the season.

It’s a great finish from Cherki to put City back in front but it doesn’t happen if Ndiaye is quick to read Danso’s risky pass and win possession. Sharp as a button in that moment.

Rayan Cherki puts Manchester City back in front! 💫 pic.twitter.com/PP4MAV9kw3

A really poor piece of defending from Kerkez gives Bournemouth a free-kick out on the right. Tavernier spins in an inswinger but Van Dijk heads clear. Truffert launches another assault on Liverpool’s box off the second phase but Alisson is wise to it and gathers.

It appears that Liverpool are beginning to settle, they take the opportunity to circulate the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure, waiting for the right moment to pounce. The final pass is poor, though, and Araujo through-pass goes all the way through to Petrovic. It was aimed at Isak ...I think.

Some signs of life from Liverpool, as they create a substantial overload down their left, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Barcola and Isak meeting on that flank. Barcola attempts a sprint into the channel off the shoulder of the ball-side centre-back but he is deemed offside. Looked close, but a bit better from Liverpool.

Araujo has the chance to launch a long throw into the box but Silva beats Van Dijk to the summit and Petrovic gathers the loose ball.

Scott then sprays a wonderful ball over to Rayan on the right but his cutback to Tavernier comes to nothing after the midfielder loses the ball. Liverpool then spring a counter of their own, but Bournemouth recover and charge down a hopeful Gakpo effort from the edge of the box.

Liverpool will not be pleased with their start to this match. They’ve struggled to string more than three passes together without ceding possession and Isak has cut an isolated figure up top.

First time that Bournemouth have gone through the gears and the move ends with Alisson Becker saving brilliantly from Evanilson. It’s a funny stadium, here, as it can be quiet then all of a sudden a tempest whips up and you can sense the mood changing. Liverpool are struggling for alacrity and Andoni Iraola is keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz, who is moving gingerly after taking a bang to his left foot.

Some start at the Etihad. You had to wonder if a big early missed chance from Nilson Angulo was going to haunt Sunderland with City taking the lead just a few minutes later through a quite sublime free-kick from Enzo Fernandez. But Sunderland have immediately hit back. Maresca will decry the defending but it’s brilliant from Enzo Le Fee, who surges forward and then splits Nunes and Dias with an inch perfect pass that Brobbey takes beautifully in his stride before finishing.

On Fernandez’s free-kick before then, he’d very much shaped as if he’s going to cross the ball from a free-kick on the right side of the penalty area. He’d clearly spotted an opening in the top right though and, while giving the firm impression to Roefs he was going to whip in a cross, he obviously had other ideas. The execution was immaculate but it was telling just how effectively he’d managed to deceive the Sunderland goalkeeper. It was world class

A slight mix-up sees Kerkez and Wirtz bump into each other by the touchline. The Germany international limps away and grimaces but should be fine to continue.

Chance! Alisson makes amends with a stunning save. Tavernier had hit the by-line and lasered a cross to Evanilson who, with the ball slightly behind him, improvised and flicked it toward the near post. Alisson gets down swiftly and turns behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Jacquet gives away a needless foul on the near side but Scott’s delivery goes straight into Alisson’s hands. The Brazilian’s throw out is poor, though, and Scott darts into Liverpool’s box, just unable to pick out a team-mate.

Barcola is presented with green grass to run into, but just as he builds a head of steam Hill comes across in a flash and snuffs out the foray forward.

Woah, Brobbey responds immediately, stealing in between City defenders before slotting past Donnarumma.

Instant response from Sunderland as Brian Brobbey equalises! 💥 pic.twitter.com/et6AHGPAbl

Enzo Fernandez opens the scoring at the Etihad with a direct free-kick from out wide. Really poor from Roefs who was caught napping. That’s Fernandez’s first City goal.

Enzo Fernandez gets his first Manchester City goal in style! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/fVOnJvACYY

Wirtz earns a free-kick just outside the D. Bournemouth feel aggrieved as there looked to have been an earlier foul on Scott and to make matters worse Szoboszlai is standing over the ball.

His effort leaves Petrovic rooted to the spot but the ball veers just wide of the mark.

Evanilson’s willingness to drop deep is asking questions of Liverpool’s centre-backs. Do they follow him and risk disrupting their backline coverage?

The hosts attempt to work a short corner routine but Truffert’s eventual through-ball is too strong and the ball rolls out for a Liverpool goal-kick.

This wouldn’t go down as a fixture you would circle for being noteworthy but make no mistake this is a huge afternoon for Liverpool. They have had some days at the Vitality Stadium in recent years and last season’s defeat put a huge dent in Arne Slot’s hopes of trying to find a revival. It’s also a big test for Bournemouth, coming down from the euphoria of beating Real Sociedad. Let’s see how it all transpires.

Evanilson makes a smart run into the right channel and while Jacquet gets his foot on the ball he’s instantly smothered by Scott and the ball goes out for a Liverpool goal-kick. A sign of how high both sides will be willing to jump in search of the ball.

Both sides will look to force mistakes out of the other and Szoboszlai is able to pick Adams’ pocket on the halfway line. He offloads to Araujo who runs into a cul de sac down the right flank.

We are under way at the Vitality. Bournemouth are in their customary black-and-red home shirts kicking from right to left and Liverpool are in their white away kit and red shorts.

The players have emerged from the tunnel, Van Dijk and Smith at the front of the lines. A few pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere but one thing missing is the accidental sitting in the wrong dugout from the returning Iraola. He knows where he’s going.

Here is a reminder of today’s squads in full:

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Barcola, Wirtz, Gakpo; IsakSubstitutes: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Tsimikas, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Munoz, Koumas, Ngumoha

The Egyptian king grabbed his first hat-trick for Trabzonspor yesterday, in a 4-0 win over league-leaders Galatasaray no less. That’s his seventh goal in eight matches.

When Salah is happy, we're all happy 👑👑👑 pic.twitter.com/DtzaOl3hD3

"He's certainly very quick"Jamie Carragher's first impressions of Bradley Barcola ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/oXjzXBuZwm

Since losing to Arsenal 3-2 on January 3, Bournemouth have not lost at the Vitality in 12 matches, picking up four wins and eight draws.

Jan 7: Bournemouth 3 Tottenham Hotspur 2Jan 24: Bournemouth 3 Liverpool 2 Feb 7: Bournemouth 1 Aston Villa 1Feb 28: Bournemouth 1 Sunderland 1Mar 3: Bournemouth 0 Brentford 0Mar 20: Bournemouth 2 Manchester United 2Apr 22: Bournemouth 2 Leeds United 2May 3: Bournemouth 3 Crystal Palace 0 May 19: Bournemouth 1 Manchester City 1Aug 29: Bournemouth 1 Everton 1Sep 8: Bournemouth 4 Lincoln City 0 (League Cup)Sep 12: Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”

Your Eagles at Elland Road 🦅 pic.twitter.com/QGBqKJoSD1

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/U0fRnjJLjv

Bournemouth signed Truffert from Rennes in the summer of 2025 to replace Kerkez – who had just joined Liverpool – and the left-back has been a revelation at the Vitality. So much so that this week he earned himself a call-up to Zinedine Zidane’s first France squad.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Virgil van Dijk says Liverpool are still a work in progress at the moment and there are a lot of positive signs ahead of their game against Bournemouth💪Watch Super Sunday live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/oSMxxIw9lQ

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”

Just the one alternation to the side Rose fielded last weekend as Christie comes in for Kluivert.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#1682. Pep Guardiola names three former midfielders he expects to become good managers, including an ex-Man City player

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:15

Pep Guardiola believes that midfielders have characteristics that can make the transition from the pitch to the technical area easier.

In an interview with Romario TV, the former Manchester City manager spoke about players who, in his view, have the potential to build a successful career as managers, and highlighted the broader vision of the game that the position requires.

Among the names mentioned are Ilkay Gundogan, Sergio Busquets and Xabi Alonso, all with midfield experience and different trajectories in football. When asked about former players who could follow in his footsteps on the touchline, Guardiola was direct in naming his picks.

'I think Gundogan will be a good manager... Busquets will be a good manager. I knew Xabi Alonso would become a good manager.'

The statement brings together three players who played important roles in elite teams and who, during their careers, played in roles that demanded game reading, tactical understanding and the ability to organise collective actions.

The choice of names follows the central idea presented by the manager. For Guardiola, experience as a midfielder can offer an especially favourable base for those who want to lead a team. That is because the position requires involvement at different moments of the match, in both attacking build-up and defensive organisation, as well as a constant understanding of the positioning of team-mates and opponents.

Guardiola explained why he sees an advantage in players who operate in that area. In the Catalan's view, the role demands a reading that goes beyond individual participation, as the midfielder needs to understand how the team moves and what each moment of the match requires.

'I think midfielders have an advantage because they need to have a more global understanding of the game' - he said.

The manager deepened his reasoning by drawing a comparison with forwards. 'They have to make the team play and understand which areas to defend. A forward often just thinks: "I am going to score a goal, and that is it."'

The observation is not a criticism of forwards, but highlights the difference in responsibilities between the positions.

While a forward can concentrate much of his performance on finishing and the pursuit of goals, the midfielder needs to follow the collective dynamic, identify spaces, take part in ball circulation and understand the movements required to protect the team without possession.

The three names cited by the manager have trajectories that help explain his assessment. Gundogan worked with Guardiola at Manchester City, while Busquets was a key part of Barcelona during the period when Guardiola managed the team. Xabi Alonso, meanwhile, was coached by Guardiola at Bayern Munich.

What they have in common, beyond the position, is that all three built careers marked by the ability to interpret the game and make decisions in different tactical contexts.

In Alonso's case, Guardiola had already shown this perception before the former midfielder began his managerial career. The Spaniard retired as a player in 2017 and later rose to prominence in charge of Bayer Leverkusen, work that reinforced the bet made by his former manager.

Gundogan and Busquets are also examples of players who, through the experience accumulated in elite football, inspire Guardiola's confidence when it comes to a possible career in management.

#1681. CM: Milan considered Maresa before Man City move – the background

Ruben Amorim became the AC Milan head coach in the summer, but he was far from the only name the management considered.

Calciomercato.com have published a report revealing some of the background on Enzo Maresca, who became Manchester City’s new manager on July 1st after an incredible successful decade under the iconic Pep Guardiola.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

“In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” said the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

“You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This shows how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he said.

“If we’re where we are, something needs to change. We need to be a little more courageous. Every time we miss a World Cup or a European Championship, people say everything needs to change, and then nothing ever changes.”

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.
