#1680. Premier League predictions: Pochettino backed to get first win on Old Trafford bow

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of another weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

The top three all dropped points last weekend, with Arsenal and Manchester City drawing with Newcastle United and Fulham, and Brighton stunned by two stoppage-time goals from Hull City.

Liverpool took advantage of that to close the gap with their 4-0 thrashing of 10-man Manchester United – with Mauricio Pochettino's disappointing start seeing the Red Devils stay in the bottom three.

Thomas Frank also got off to a losing start at Crystal Palace, who remain bottom of the table, after a 3-2 loss to Coventry City in his first game.

Matchday 12 sees fixtures take place across Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Ahead of what should be another intriguing set of Premier League games, let's check out the Opta supercomputer’s match predictions.

The weekend kicks off at the City Ground on Friday, with Nottingham Forest and Chelsea both looking to get back to winning ways.

Since the start of March, no side has lost more Premier League games than Chelsea (13), who were beaten by Sunderland and Leeds United in their last two outings. Similarly, among ever-present sides, only Crystal Palace (17) have earned fewer points than the Blues (23) over the same period.

Chelsea are at least unbeaten in their last five away league games against Forest (W4 D1), winning each of the last three, though our predictive model gives them just a 33.5% chance of stretching that run to four.

Forest, who won 39.9% of the pre-match simulations, are looking to win consecutive league games against Chelsea for the first time since April 1979, though there is also a 26.6% chance of a draw.

#1679. Barcelona's Anthony Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes' against Sabah as Spanish media hail England international on historic night

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 09:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 09:29

Anthony Gordon scored twice in Barcelona's 4-1 win over Sabah in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

In doing so, Gordon made history - the forward has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the England international's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice against Sabah on Wednesday.

Lamine Yamal missed out through injury, while Raphinha was rested from the start, with Gordon joined by Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus in the final third, and all three found the back of the net.

As expected, Gordon's performance brought a lot of praise from the Spanish media.

6 - Anthony Gordon's six UEFA Champions League goals in Azerbaijan are the most any English player has scored in away games in one country in the competition. Tourist. https://t.co/7OfdYkdzch

AS were extremely positive about Gordon's performance, saying that the forward was 'vital' to Barcelona securing all three points in the Champions League.

Mundo Deportivo also highlighted how well he combined with Gabriel Jesus and Adeyemi in the final third of the field in the absence of Yamal and Raphinha.

La Vanguardia concentrated on how Gordon became the main player in the Barcelona attack and said that he was one of the main reasons why Hansi Flick's side were able to score four goals.

Culemania said that Gordon 'stepped into Raphinha's shoes', having netted twice in the absence of the Brazil international, who has scored 19 times in all competitions this season.

Gordon will never be the main man in the Barcelona attack due to the presence of both Yamal and Raphinha, but he has played an important supporting role this term.

The 25-year-old's numbers for this season are relatively solid, coming up with five goals and five assists in 17 appearances in all competitions.

In La Liga, Gordon has two goals and five assists in 12 appearances, while he has struck three times in five outings in the Champions League.

The forward will be looking to improve his goal total in Spain's top flight, but it has been a positive start to his Barcelona career for the former Everton youngster.

#1678. Paul Scholes says 'rabbit in headlights' Leny Yoro is not 'Premier League level' - as Nicky Butt claims this Man United side are the 'most unathletic team' in their history with only THREE players able to run at Anfield

Published: 16:03 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:05 EST, 23 November 2026

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has become the latest ex-Red Devil to tear into the club's defence, criticising Leny Yoro following his red card in his side's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's clash with their rivals at Anfield on Sunday, tripping Alexander Isak as he ran in on goal after an error from Matthijs de Ligt.

He has had a mixed time of things since his £52million move to Old Trafford in 2024, though has been playing in a leaky United defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches this season – with only Crystal Palace conceding more.

Several different members of United's defence have come under fire this season, and, on Monday, it was the turn of Yoro.

'The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him,' Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football, sponsored by Midnite.

He added: 'You know what, he’s come in to a really bad setup defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to (Virgil) Van Dijk he might look a little bit better but he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights.'

Paul Scholes (pictured) has suggested Leny Yoro is not yet ready for the Premier League

Yoro was sent off in the opening minutes of Manchester United's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool

Fellow former United midfielder Nicky Butt, who played alongside Scholes for United between 1994 and 2004, added: 'If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea. He’s a great talent that will come good.'

Scholes, though, wasn't having any of it.

He replied: 'I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is. I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races. Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, oh, what do I do?'

United have also faced criticism for their apparent lack of running this season, with eyebrows raised when Youri Tielemans said in the summer that they didn't do much prior to the campaign getting under way.

The club rank 17th for distance covered in the top flight this season, with Liverpool, Brentford and Everton below them. The latter two will almost certainly pass them though after their game on Monday.

That, according to Butt, is down to the players.

'We’ve had our say about the players and they’re just not good enough,' he said. 'It is the most unathletic team I’ve ever seen in Man United.

'I’m going to go through a team and I’m trying to be as honest as I can. Forget the quality for right now. For me, physicality-wise, if you go through a team, the right back, he’s physically OK, but he’s not amazing. De Ligt or Harry, whoever he’s going to play in there, physically not great. Martinez for me is physically not great. You got Yoro who will physically come good.

Nicky Butt (pictured), meanwhile, has criticised the physical ability of many of United's players

'Then I go on to the midfield, none of them are physically good enough. Kobbie can get about the pitch 15-20 yards, but he’s not box to box. Said that numerous times. He’s got a lot of talent. He’s got a lot of things going for him. I think he’s a top player. He ain’t got the legs. He needs to have legs around him but his legs around him at the minute are Bruno and Tielemans - and they can’t run around.

'Look at Mbeumo, I think he’s OK but he’s not going to blow anybody away. I think Cunha can run. So then you look at the whole squad and you’re saying three players can run.

'What I’m getting at there, and it sounds like I’m being a draconian but what you have to do first and foremost when you go to Anfield is to be able to compete physically and they can’t so they have no chance.'

#1677. GdS: Amorim to field strong side vs. Olympiacos in bid to fix Europa League struggles

AC Milan will head to Greece on Thursday with the need to overturn a negative trend, so Ruben Amorim will leave nothing to chance.

In the past few weeks (barring the international break), Milan have alternated good performances at weekends with disastrous midweek results. The collapse against Bologna is one example, while losses to Bournemouth and Ferencvaros have complicated the Europa League mission.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Amorim won’t be opting for the usual excessive rotation against Olympiacos on Thursday night in Athens. There will be some changes, but the coach will field several regular starters.

The paper report that Amorim knows full well that victory is the only acceptable result in order for the Rossoneri to get back on track in their big to qualify for at least the Europa League play-offs, with the top eight now a distant mirage.

The Portuguese will rest Luka Modric in midfield. He will be replaced by Ardon Jashari, who scored his first goal for the Rossoneri in the win over Genoa. Adrien Rabiot – the Rossoneri’s driving force in this first part of the season – will remain in the team.

The defensive choices are almost forced, with Koni De Winter and Sankhoun Diawara still the centre-backs. Strahinja Pavlovic is not yet 100% fit and will undergo further tests on the kidney stone issues that have kept him out for the last month, even though he played 20 minutes on Sunday.

Up front, the same attack that played against Frosinone should be seen, namely Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira supporting Gonçalo Ramos, who finally returned to scoring after more than a month without a goal.

Both Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchison are raring to go, but both are expected to start on the bench in Athens, ready to come on as substitutes. Beyond the players, it will be crucial for Milan to take to the pitch with the right attitude.

#1676. Leeds United news: Major Dominic Calvert-Lewin contract update ahead of January window?

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 09:38

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has reportedly signed a new Leeds United contract running until the summer of 2029.

Daniel Farke's side have continued their excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign following the November international break, recording a 4-1 success at the Stamford Bridge home of Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

As a result of Lukas Nmecha and company collecting maximum points from the West London contest, the Elland Road club have stayed in seventh position in the Premier League standings, on the coattails of the Champions League conversation.

The main man in attack for Leeds in recent times, Calvert-Lewin has made a positive start to the season, with the 29-year-old Leeds star supposedly wanted by relegation-threatened Manchester United.

Nevertheless, the England international will be fully focused on helping Farke's troops qualify for European competition this term, with the Whites welcoming Coventry City to Yorkshire on Saturday.

According to The Athletic's Beren Cross via transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Leeds United supporters have been given a major piece of positive news regarding the future of leading marksman Calvert-Lewin.

The report claims that the 29-year-old has agreed to an extension of his current terms at Elland Road, with the Three Lions appearance-maker originally joining on a free transfer from Everton in August 2025.

It is understood that Calvert-Lewin's fresh deal will run until the conclusion of the 2028-29 campaign, at which point the striker will be heading towards his mid-30s and the twilight of his career.

Before Leeds can officially announce the news surrounding the forward, it is believed that they must complete 'formal steps', with everyone involved in the process expecting a smooth process in that respect.

Either side of the November international break, Calvert-Lewin's side have recorded back-to-back wins over Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, proving their strength against some of the Premier League's biggest names.

Part of the furniture in the Premier League since the 2017-18 campaign, Calvert-Lewin has been the classic example of a confidence and purple-patch striker, with the attacker's form swinging dramatically.

This season, the 29-year-old is arguably churning out the best performances of his top-flight career to date, scoring five goals and providing one assist during the opening 11 Premier League games.

Whilst Leeds are known to be in the market for another striker ahead of the January window, there is no desire to replace Calvert-Lewin in the starting XI, as is clear with a contract extension on the table.

#1675. Marmoush backs Spurs youngster Williams-Barnett to have ‘very big future’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Omar Marmoush has backed his "unbelievable" Tottenham team-mate Luca Williams-Barnett to have a "very big future".

The teenager has impressed under Roberto De Zerbi in recent weeks, most notably scoring and assisting in their Premier League win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Aged 18 years and 51 days, Williams-Barnett became the second-youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game, behind Michael Owen.

He also became the fourth-youngest player to score on his first Premier League start, behind Daniel Jebbison in May 2021 (17y 276d), Danny Cadamarteri in September 1997 (17y 343d) and Mark Cullen in May 2010 (18y 12d).

Should he start and score against Sunderland on Sunday, he'd be the youngest player to score in his first two starts (18 years, 59 days).

The forward's breakthrough into the Spurs' first team was rewarded with a new contract, which is reported to be a five-year deal, and Marmoush believes the only way is up for the exciting winger.

"He is unbelievable," Marmoush told Sky sports about Williams-Barnett.

It's always been Tottenham. https://t.co/W3mx3ZQIH9

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 24, 2026

"He is a great, great talent and what I like most about him, of course, his talent is something that everyone sees, is that he is very brave, too.

"And when he came on in his first game, he just took the ball and tried things. He is very direct, tries to beat his opponent and he has a very, very promising future ahead of him.

"He has got it, and you can see that. One of the big traits of a big talent, and a big player, is the personality and the character and that is what stands out most for me, his courage and to be brave.

"As a young lad, to come into Spurs' first team and perform like that is not easy, and just to believe in yourself and do the actions on your pitch is great.

"I hope he is enjoying it, and he will have a very, very big future, that's for sure."

#1674. Liverpool: With Isak and Wirtz, the Reds’ transfer business takes off a year late

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 09:44

During the 2025 summer transfer window, Liverpool broke the bank, spending £410m.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were the two most expensive signings, as the Swedish striker arrived for £123m (€145m) and the German attacking midfielder for £106m (€125m). But for many months, the two most expensive recruits in the club's history failed to live up to expectations.

In his first season at Liverpool, Wirtz scored seven goals and provided 10 assists in 49 games, but his impact was largely disappointing. Isak, for his part, barely played (four goals and one assist in 22 games) because of a fractured fibula. That summer 2025 transfer window was thus described as 'the worst transfer window in Premier League history'.

Both attackers were therefore expected to deliver in their second season at Liverpool, with new manager Andoni Iraola arriving.

The momentum is completely different at the start of this campaign, as the 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night in the Champions League illustrated perfectly. Isak scored twice, while Wirtz also found the net.

The Swede is rediscovering the efficiency that made his reputation at Newcastle United. He now has ten goals in all competitions in 16 games and has just scored in six consecutive away games for Liverpool. The 27-year-old is establishing himself as the number nine Liverpool had long been waiting for.

On Wednesday night, Isak was asked about when he would be back at his best level: 'It is always difficult to say, but I can definitely say that I feel good, the team is in a good rhythm, that is the most important thing' - he said.

After a season of adaptation to English football, in which he struggled to have an impact in the final third and to be decisive, Wirtz is in excellent form.

Still deployed as a number 10, the 23-year-old German has scored four goals and provided five assists in 17 games in all competitions for Liverpool.

His November has been excellent: three goals and two assists in three games for Liverpool, as well as three goals in two games for the German national team. Wirtz appears to have digested his huge transfer and to be ready to shed his 'flop' label at Liverpool.

“Confirmation has arrived, and I would say finally, also from Germany of something we have been telling you for weeks: Markus Krosche will be the new Head of Football at Milan. In Germany there has been a much slower narrative, much more, let’s say, Eintracht-centric,” he said (via MilanNews).

#1671. Paris Saint-Germain vs. Lorient - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45

Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.

The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.

PSG had maintained a perfect record across all competitions for nearly three months before Roma visited in the Champions League in midweek, with the Serie A side battling to a 2-2 draw on matchday five.

That result ended the Parisians' four-match European winning streak, although Luis Enrique's men remain second in the league-phase standings and firmly inside the coveted top-eight places that guarantee last-16 qualification.

Returning to league action should please supporters, who have watched their side claim eight consecutive victories since losing to Monaco at the start of September, albeit with only three clean sheets.

However, eagle-eyed observers will note that the Red and Blues have won only one of their last five meetings with Lorient across the past four years, with three of the last four encounters ending level.

Another draw would please Paris FC, Lille and Lyon, who trail the capital club by three, five and six points respectively as the Ligue 1 title race begins to take shape.

Alexandre Dujeux therefore aims to prevent Lorient's first defeat in this fixture since April 2024; however, his own five-match winless record against PSG and four consecutive losses to Enrique are ominous signs for the 50-year-old manager.

An indifferent run of results further undermines confidence in Les Merlus extending their unbeaten sequence in this fixture, with the Brittany-based club winning only one of their last four league matches.

Admittedly, only one of those matches ended in defeat, a 2-0 home loss to Brest, while their solitary victory during that period came away at Le Havre.

However, that early-November success offers limited encouragement given that it came against the division's bottom side, who have collected a paltry two points from 11 matches.

Their overall away record is more encouraging, with Dujeux's team conceding just twice across five matches on the road, both in September's 2-1 defeat to Le Mans, while keeping clean sheets in the other four.

Another shutout would make Lorient the first team since Monaco in November last year to prevent PSG from scoring, a feat far easier said than done.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue are both sidelined with ACL injuries for PSG's fixture on Saturday.

Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos are pushing for their first starts since last month's 4-2 victory over Barcelona, although Enrique may be tempted to retain the centre-back partnership of Ilya Zabarnyi and Willian Pacho.

Ferran Torres remains the capital club's leading Ligue 1 scorer with five goals, while Achraf Hakimi, Senny Mayulu and Marquinhos have three apiece.

Lorient have shared the goals around this season, with nine different players finding the net for the Brittany-based visitors.

Only Jean-Victor Makengo has scored more than once for Les Merlus, leaving Dujeux searching for someone to step up at Parc des Princes.

The visitors' prospects are further weakened by the absence of Panos Katseris, with a muscle injury ruling their leading goal provider out of this weekend's encounter.

Isaak Toure (groin) and Bandiougou Fadiga (muscle) are also sidelined for the 10th-placed side on matchday 12.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:

Safonov; Hakimi, Pacho, Marquinhos, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Godts

Mvogo; Adjei, Talbi, Obaretin; Sylla, Cadiou, Ebong, Kouassi; Makengo, Bernardeau; Tosin

Lorient's four clean sheets from five away matches suggest that PSG may need patience, particularly against opponents who have repeatedly frustrated them in recent meetings.

However, the visitors' limited scoring threat and Katseris's absence should allow Enrique's men to sustain pressure and eventually secure a ninth consecutive league victory.

#1670. Dundee manager Steven Pressley wanted to 'crawl under a rock and hide' after humiliation by Hearts

Published: 16:26 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:50 EST, 23 November 2026

Dundee manager Steven Pressley is nothing if not honest. Having taken full responsibility for his team’s 8-0 thrashing by Hearts on Saturday, he now admits that the experience left him wanting to ‘crawl under a rock and hide’.

You won’t hear him writing it off as a ‘bad day at the office’ or branding it a freak result from which he and his players would quickly move on. Dundee’s heaviest-ever home defeat in the league was an indignity that really hit their popular manager. And hit him hard.

‘It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours,’ said Pressley. ‘There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

‘It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this: I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

‘I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading. But I’ve had to show strength. I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

‘We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.’

Dundee boss Steven Pressley says he felt hurt and embarrassed after losing 8-0 to Hearts

Defender Ryan Astley struggles to take in Dundee's heaviest-ever home defeat in the league

That process starts tomorrow night against Hibs, who suffered a humiliation of their own when they lost 4-0 at home to Dundee United on Saturday. Pressley says the immediate objective for his team is to go there with a better attitude than they have shown lately.

He had feared a setback coming for Dundee – ‘not 8-0 but a disappointing performance’ – because he had ‘sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency’. He felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

‘We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,’ he said. ‘We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

‘And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team. We have to be at our absolute best to get results.’

He hopes the Hearts game will be ‘a reset moment’ that eventually helps his players to improve, but there are no guarantees from Pressley that they will shake it off at Easter Road tomorrow.

Asked if he expected a positive response from them, he said: ‘I don’t know. I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

‘But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.’

The good news for Dundee is that they are up against a team who have been hopeless in their own stadium recently. Second-bottom Hibs have lost nine of their last ten Premiership games at Easter Road and haven’t taken three points there since early April.

Supporters turned on the Edinburgh side after the defeat by Dundee United, but Hibs midfielder Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea that he and his team-mates don’t enjoy playing in their own ground.

Jamie McGrath was in the Hibs side that suffered another defeat at Easter Road on Saturday

‘Personally, I always like playing at home,’ said McGrath. ‘I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a big open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

‘It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb.’

It looked like Marink Reedijk’s side had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

So McGrath is hoping Saturday’s aberration was a blip. ‘We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us. We were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams. It’s frustrating not to build on that.’

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs’ lowly league position and senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

‘It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute. It’s obviously not where we want to be. We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.’

#1669. Fabregas shares thoughts on Alvini’s approach with Frosinone in Milan drubbing

Cesc Fabregas has praised Massimiliano Alvini for the way he set Frosinone up against AC Milan, despite their heavy defeat.

There has been a divided narrative after Milan put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro on Sunday night, the team that have been one of the surprise packages in Serie A so far this season. Some feel Alvini was too aggressive in his approach, while others praised his unwavering principles.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is not too dissimilar to some of the discourse that has followed Fabregas around early in his coaching career. The exchange between the Spaniard and Massimiliano Allegri made the headlines last season, after Milan’s more pragmatic approach yielded four points against the Lariani.

Speaking at a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against AEK Athens, Fabregas also answered a question about his style of play and gave a nod to Alvini. His words are via MilanPress.

“I want to continue to hear that Alvini is a great coach. He is. In the press conference he said he’ll never change, and for me that means identity, courage, and knowing what you want to do,” he began.

“It’s very important, even when you win or lose 1-0 or not. You’re not bad when you lose, you’re not a phenomenon when you win. I’ll do the same as he did against Milan, I’ll stick with my ideas.

“Obviously, there are games where you don’t play well, you have to know how to manage them when you’re not at your best. But I can’t change everything that’s good here.”

#1668. Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

On TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their new head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

United’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M

But, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so important for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

In the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

It was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

It was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

The defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm

Fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. It is just one win in five for United, and it was another performance which was far from convincing. It could have been worse though, they were a few minutes away from losing. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

United break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

United may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M

Bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

United with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

You would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

Here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

Positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

Fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

Fulham have stopped playing since they scored, and they needed Leno again to tip a Cunha shot around the post. The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

What a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”

Well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN

Fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

Fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

Gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the new season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

More from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”

There has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

Sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

At half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

United’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

This stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

If Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

JJ Gabriel has been in the news this week, and Sam Wallace writes in his column this week that the battle to sign up and coming academy players is growing ever more fierce between Premier League clubs. Managers are handing out debuts earlier and earlier to satisfy the demands of the best young players, and an increasing number of clubs are happy to gamble significant fees and wages on potental.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia

Subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊

The script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager said.

“That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1666. GdS: Strong bonds, Ramos and signings – five reasons for Milan to believe in the Scudetto

AC Milan are five points behind the somewhat surprise league-leaders Lazio, but belief is growing regarding a Scudetto push.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan re-emerged from the two-week international break and put in arguably their best performance of the season against Frosinone. They scored five goals and it could have been more, racking up a third league win in a row to move back into the top four.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The table remains quite tight at the top, with Inter the only team to slip up over the weekend, and the Rossoneri are firmly in the running. The paper highlights give reasons that a title fight is very possible.

Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim are inextricably linked, and that might seem obvious, given that one is the owner and the other the coach. In reality, the bond is deeper than usual, for one simple reason.

Amorim has been handed the keys to create the ‘new Milan’, one that Cardinale has decided to manage completely differently since the end of May. The Portuguese is the coach to whom RedBird have given the longest contract so far, and Cardinale believes he’s the right man at the right time.

He’s demonstrating this concretely not only with his constant presence and his reassuring words, but also with his intention to improve the squad quickly and with the arrival of a key management figure like Markus Krösche. Now, Amorim will receive even greater support.

Gonçalo Inacio, Nicolo Tresoldi, Endrick. These are just some of the names circulating – and these aren’t rumours, but actual targets – ahead of a potentially crucial January transfer window.

The question is obvious: with a couple of top-notch signings for the second half of the season, how far could this team go? Staying up there for starters remains the minimum objective, with Champions League football a must.

Then, Amorim and co. hope that the rest will follow, if their rivals begin to lose pace. The coach is starting to make his team look like they are clicking, but Cardinale has realised the need to accelerate to fill the remaining gaps in the squad.

Amorim (fortunately) quickly realised that the average tactical level of his colleagues in Italy is too high to allow himself to present his Milan team in the same way every single way. So, the 3-4-2-1 that was previously seemingly set in stone has become plasticine in his hands.

The manager moulds and shapes the playing system based on the opponents, rather than his own needs. Since Ruben the fundamentalist became Ruben the quick-change artist, we’ve seen a bit of everything: 4-2-3-1, 4-3-3, 4-4-1-1, 3-5-2.

The former Sporting CP coach coach locks himself in the lab throughout the week and tailors the formation he deems best. Sometimes he gets it wrong, but most of the time he gets it right.

Milan have won five of their last six league games and, game by game, they are increasingly able to camouflage themselves effectively tactically. Opponents never know what formation they will face, while Amorim has several players capable of playing well in multiple roles, which helps.

The data is remarkable and reads as follows: only Rocco (29) and Czeizler (31) coached Milan sides that have scored more goals than Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 Serie A games in charge.

In short, despite all the problems involved (Goncalo Ramos in particular, more on him to come) the coach’s attacking vocation is clearly visible. Furthermore, it is a Milan with a high conversion rate in proportion to the shots on target.

It is also a Diavolo side that have somehow found a way to make up for Ramos’ poor contribution in terms of goals. Alphadjo Cisse, Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot take turns to set each other up and score, a sign of a growing offensive physiognomy.

More often than not, a striker simply needs to get a goal in order to build confidence and then begin a virtuous cycle. Milan hope that this is the case for Ramos, who ended his month-long goal drought on Sunday.

However, the reflection goes further: while the Rossoneri having the luxury of being able to score without goals from their No.9 (who is currently on three in the league), surely things can only get better from here?

In short, if the Portuguese international actually does start firing more regularly, then Milan might unlock another dimension to their attack that could really see them surge towards that elusive Scudetto.

#1665. Man United urged to sign £62.8m midfielder to fix "phenomenal" transfer mistakes (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 10:16

Former Manchester United star Gordon Strachan - speaking exclusively to Sports Mole - has urged the Red Devils to sign a £62.8m midfielder to help correct their "phenomenal" transfer mistakes.

New Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino remains winless since replacing Michael Carrick following Wednesday's infuriating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, in which the Red Devils fell behind, took the lead and were then pegged back in Portugal.

The four-goal stalemate marked the seventh game in a row that Man United had conceded at least two goals, and once again, the Red Devils' open midfield was exposed.

The pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo did not cover themselves in glory against Liverpool or Sporting, and the former is now suspended for RB Leipzig in December after being sent off towards the end of Wednesday's game.

Andrey Santos has also not yet had the desired impact since joining from Chelsea, while fellow 22-year-old Carlos Baleba has played just 397 minutes across seven appearances due to injury problems.

Speaking to Sports Mole via William Hill betting site, Strachan - who scored 36 goals in 198 games for Man United - has told the Red Devils hierarchy to make a move for Crystal Palace lynchpin Adam Wharton to help offset the "phenomenal" amount of money the club has wasted on under-performing players.

"Adam Wharton is one of my picks," Strachan said. "Elliot Anderson was also another one they should have gone for. Tielemans has been doing well in the Premier League for nearly 10 years, so they're buying somebody who's at the latter stage of his career. I might be wrong, I hope I'm wrong, and hopefully, he’s got another five or six years in him.

"And I've got to say, the world of football in England is full of the top teams, especially Chelsea, Spurs, bringing in players who sign for £40m, £50m, you go, who is he? There's just so many players like this now.

"You see some of these players, and you go, what has he done to deserve a £45m fee? Baleba, Santos, you’re picking up people for big fees, who have no reputation.

"Who's been brave here? Is this just a kind of cosy midfield? You could go back to Mason Mount for £40m - who actually signed this off to pay this amount of money for players?

"It’s just beyond belief the money that Man United have wasted. It's phenomenal. And that's from the recruitment not doing their work properly.

"They've got to start saying, what is my plan for the next 10 years at Man United? And how do we go about this? Arsenal were a bit like that five or six years ago. It wasn't anywhere near as bad a situation as Man United, but they stuck to their plan, and it paid off."

Data from the 2026-27 season does not paint Wharton in the most positive light compared to his Man United peers, given Crystal Palace's atrocious start to the campaign.

Indeed, the England international only leads Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Mainoo on games played, crosses per 90 and accurate crosses per 90, while also winning the fewest duels and registering the lowest percentage of successful passes.

However, Wharton has committed the fewest fouls per 90 minutes of the quintet, and he has been dispossessed on the second-fewest occasions per 90 minutes, only behind Santos.

Thanks to Crystal Palace's perilous position in the Premier League table - Thomas Frank's men sit bottom of the rankings with just seven points from nine games - interested parties could pick up Wharton for a discount if the Eagles are relegated to the Championship.

The 22-year-old is valued at €75m (£62.8m) by Transfermarkt and has three years left on his Palace contract, but Man United may have to fend off competition from Liverpool and Chelsea to land him in 2027.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

#1664. Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026

As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.

If 2026 felt like it had been shaping up to be something of an annus horribilis, a 4-2 victory at Rugby Park undoubtedly lifted some of the gloom that had been hanging over the club these past few months.

Granted, a sample size of only one match under Mario Frick is very small. Nobody would be of a mind to get carried away with themselves just yet, especially given that Killie are easily the worst team in the league.

But there was enough in the performance, particularly during a first half which saw them score three goals in 30 minutes, to suggest that a brighter future could lie ahead under the new manager.

Aberdeen were aggressive, they played on the front foot, and they attacked with pace. Most of all, they were actually exciting and entertaining to watch.

Those were boxes they never ticked at any point during Stephen Robinson's time in charge. Robinson failed at Aberdeen and his team were routinely awful in terms of the quality of football they served up.

Mario Frick celebrates after a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock in his first game as Aberdeen manager

Ante Palaversa is back in the Aberdeen team after becoming the forgotten man of Pittodrie

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet rediscovered the feelgood factor by scoring twice at Rugby Park

In the space of only 90 minutes, Frick did more to send a wave of positivity through supporters than Robinson ever managed to do in his eight months at the helm.

The shift in mood has been as profound as it has been instantaneous, with Frick's so-called heavy metal football music to the fans' ears.

Headlines of Super Mario were always likely to follow, but Frick and his players will face an altogether tougher examination when they take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow.

It is an intriguing contest on various levels, with Rangers unbeaten in 13 matches as Derek McInnes goes up against his former club once again.

Given that these teams met in the Premier Sports Cup only a few weeks ago, perhaps the greatest barometer of Frick's impact will be whether Aberdeen can pose more of a threat than they did at Hampden.

But what has changed? After such a turgid run of form that left players looking completely bereft of any confidence and cohesion, how was Frick able to generate an immediate improvement?

Speaking after the win at Killie, Frick was asked what sort of message he had given to the players given that time together on the training pitch had been fairly limited.

'I told them they should play like they did when they were young. In those days they didn't think about mistakes.

'They didn't think about anything negative. They played only to win, for fun.'

It was simple but refreshing. In an age of increasingly complex coaching jargon, Frick's message was intended to liberate his players – and it worked a treat.

Aberdeen went 2-0 up inside 12 minutes, with Kevin Nisbet scoring twice. The team looked free from the trauma of the Robinson era.

Even when Kilmarnock fought back and the game became more chaotic, Aberdeen retained enough attacking threat and collective belief to close it out.

It was a huge result. A defeat would have dropped Aberdeen to the foot of the table. Instead, they climbed five places and, more importantly, rediscovered a feelgood factor.

In his previous utterances, Frick was clear that goalscoring has been the central problem.

His previous teams at Vaduz and Luzern were known for their attacking output. At Luzern last season they scored 76 goals.

Aberdeen had managed only 12 in 12 league matches before his arrival. The early evidence suggests the players have absorbed the message quickly.

Frick's insistence on the basics – aggression, willingness to work, positive body language – appears to have cut through more effectively than more elaborate instructions might have done.

This is consistent with the picture painted by those who worked with him in Switzerland. Frick is not a rigid systems coach wedded to a single formation.

He has most often used a 4-4-2 diamond, but the shape is secondary to the mentality. High pressing to force turnovers, rapid counter-attacks, and a sense of freedom imbued to his players.

All of which makes tomorrow's clash at Ibrox all the more compelling. Aberdeen have lost their last eight meetings with Rangers in all competitions.

The previous two encounters this season, one in the Premiership and one in the Premier Sports Cup, were both settled by late Rangers goals.

The contrast in styles will be stark. Rangers are likely to control territory and force Aberdeen to defend for longer periods than they did at Rugby Park.

Frick's side will need to show that the freedom he has granted them does not dissolve into naivety when the opponent is stronger and more experienced.

The high press that worked so effectively against a struggling Killie side will have to be timed with greater precision.

The attacking play will require clinical decision-making in the final third. And the defensive structure, which Frick identified as the main area for improvement after Saturday, will be examined under more sustained pressure.

Frick has already spoken of aiming higher than mere survival. In a league which is always extremely tight in the mid-table, top six should be the minimum target.

That may have sounded optimistic a fortnight ago. But the win at Kilmarnock suggested Aberdeen have enough about themselves to be looking up rather than over their shoulders.

The squad still needs greater consistency and, in certain areas, greater quality.

But there is already evidence to suggest he can get a tune out of some players who either under-performed under Robinson or, in some cases, those who had been totally discarded.

Ante Palaversa would surely be chief among them. The Croatian midfielder hardly kicked a ball under Robinson and had become the forgotten man at Pittodrie.

Brought in to make his first league start of the season, his performance at Killie and the way he controlled things in midfield made his exclusion under Robinson look all the more bizarre.

None of this is to say that Aberdeen are suddenly a top-class football team. At best, they remain very much a work in progress.

Yet, crucially, Frick immediately has the supporters onboard in a way that Robinson never managed to do.

Frick and his players could yet be given a major reality check if they were to suffer a hefty defeat to a Rangers side unbeaten in 13 matches.

But there is belief and positivity in the camp at Pittodrie. Feelgood factors in football can often be fragile and often short-lived, but they are also real.

When players begin to play with freedom and confidence, results usually tend to take care of themselves.

Frick has not yet transformed Aberdeen. He has, however, given the players and the fans a reason to believe that a brighter future could lie ahead.

#1663. Bayern sporting director rules out big January spending

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund insisted they are not planning "anything big" in the January transfer window, despite their recent injury crisis.

Vincent Kompany's side were dealt two major blows in their Bundesliga draw with Koln last week after both Harry Kane and Michael Olise went down with injuries.

While Olise's knock is not deemed to be serious, Kane is set to miss at least three months of action after having surgery on his ankle.

Both players missed Bayern's Champions League defeat to Lille on Wednesday, with Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer also sidelined for the loss.

Luis Diaz did make his return after a month out, but Bayern's new-look attack stuttered against Lille.

Konrad Laimer started as a makeshift striker, with Lennart Karl, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Nathaniel Brown featuring behind the Austrian.

Nineteen-year-olds Noah Codjo-Evora and Tim Binder came off the bench, but the Bundesliga champions were only able to accumulate 0.95 expected goals (xG) from their 12 shots.

#1662. Bournemouth vs. Celta Vigo: How the Cherries could equal Chelsea, Leeds feat with Europa League victory

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27

Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.

Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.

However, with the Cherries set for a Celta Vigo challenge on Thursday night, it is clear that the Dean Court club are thriving, with the visitors to Spain sitting in fifth position in the Premier League standings.

A star of the current positive form, Evanilson has truly announced himself as an elite top-flight striker, netting seven goals and providing two assists in his past eight appearances, scoring in five consecutive league fixtures.

What makes Bournemouth's run even more impressive is that last season's star man Junior Kroupi has barely started a competitive match so far after recovering from a broken leg sustained over the summer.

Starting with a 3-0 Europa League success over Austrian side Sturm Graz on October 15, Bournemouth have recorded nine straight victories in all competitions across the Premier League, EFL Cup and European action.

That winning streak is the longest since the Cherries became a Football League club at the beginning of the 1923-24 season, showcasing how impressively the South Coast team are performing at the moment.

However, there are still more records to be achieved over the coming weeks, with Bournemouth aiming to become only the eighth team to record 10 straight competitive victories whilst playing in the Premier League.

Winning the Premier League during the 2016-17 campaign under Antonio Conte, Chelsea managed 10 wins in a row in all competitions, with that particular streak running from October 2016 until New Year's Eve 2016.

Leeds are the other club to post that exact number of wins in succession, with the Elland Road side completing the feat between August and October during the 1999-00 Premier League term.

The dominant force in English domestic football during the late 2010s and early 2020s, Manchester City are unsurprisingly the club with the most consecutive competitive wins as a Premier League side.

Under the expert stewardship of Pep Guardiola, the title-winning Citizens won 21 straight matches between December 2020 and March 2021, destroying Arsenal's previous record of 13 games in succession.

To match Man City's record, Bournemouth would need to secure victory in Spain on Thursday before winning every single match up to and including the trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on January 5.
